newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on weather and exports, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on weather and exports, funds.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on rain delayed harvest in Texas and Oklahoma plus fund short covering, traders said.

"Funds were buying back their shorts," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man International. "They (harvest crews) harvested up until about noon Sunday with excellent quality. But they (commercials and elevators) did buy a lot of wheat at up eight cents today."
Wet weather moved into the U.S. Great Plains Sunday which stalled wheat harvesting.
Some said wheat export news was supportive.
USDA Monday said wheat inspected for export during the week ended June 5 totaled 15.839 million bushels, above expectations for eight to 12 million bushels.
In early dealings there was scattered talk about potential disease problems in the soft red winter crop but the market remained skeptical.
Traders were watching reports from this week's tour of the U.S. soft red winter wheat growing region. The wheat crop in Northwest Ohio is better than a year ago, the tour group said.
Wheat closed five to nine cents per bushel higher, with July up eight at $3.67-1/2.
Prudential Securities bought three million bushels of July, Rosenthal Collins bought two million July and SAK Futures bought 1.5 million July, traders said.
Dean Witter sold 1.5 million July and Refco Inc sold 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 28,000 contracts, above the 21,574 traded Friday.

In wheat options, Merrill Lynch Futures sold 200 July $3.60 puts at five to 5-1/4 cents, Smith Barney sold 200 July $3.40 puts at one to 1-1/4 cents and ING Derivatives bought 100 September $3.80 calls at 16 cents.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, above the 5,603 traded Friday.
